To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in SHR the excess accumulation of collagen occurs in the absence of myocardial hypertrophy and that the excess accumulation of myocardial collagen leads to an increase in passive stiffness of the left ventricle.

the collagen matrix of hypertensive rats is remodeled in the absence of cell hypertrophy, which suggests that the collagenous and muscular compartments of the myocardial are under separate controls, and that the excess accumulation of collagen leads to abnormal passive myocardial stiffness, which can be prevented by hydralazine.

1) the collagen volume fraction of SHR was increased by 2.7 fold, 2) hydralazine treatment of SHR reduced LV mass by 17% but had no effect on collagen accumulation, 3) the collagen content of the LV was not related to LV mass in either SHR or SHRT and 4) the collagen content was increased by 50% in SHRT compared to WKY.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of collagen to the development of cardiac hypertrophy and the effect of hypertrophy on the passive mechanical properties of the myocardium.
the relationship between myocardial collagen, hypertrophy, and mechanics in the spontaneously hypertensive rat.
the relationship of myocardial collagen to myocardial function and the role of this relationship in the development of heart failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
collagen remodeling is a major component of cardiac hypertrophy and that this remodeling can be dissociated from the development of hypertrophy.
collagenous remodeling occurs in the absence of LV hypertrophy and that such remodeling is associated with abnormal passive stiffness and reduced active stiffness of the myocardium.
the myocardium of SHRT is not normal, but is less abnormal than that of SHR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the collagen matrix of the myocardium can be modified in the absence of cell death or hypertrophy, but that this modification is associated with an abnormal passive stiffness.

in SHR the myocardium is in a state of hypertrophy with abnormal collagen remodeling and that the prevention of hypertrophic growth with hydralizine reduces active myocardial stiffness but not the abnormal collagen remodeling.
the myocardial hypertrophy and the excess accumulation of collagen are not the only factors contributing to the increased myocardial stiffness observed in hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen remodeling that occurs in hypertension is not simply the result of hypertrophy, and that the prevention of hypertrophic growth does not eliminate the excess collagen deposition.
collagen remodeling can occur independently of myocardial hypertrophy and cell death, leading to abnormal passive stiffness.
the collagen matrix is a dynamic entity and can change independently from the muscle.
